requirement: The bundled skills MUST direct agents to describe sites exactly as the site queries select them, to state as an obligation any convention the queries rely on, such as how a list is named, and to state only per-site obligations that a reviewer can check from the site and the helpers it calls.
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.site_text` has three clauses. The bundled skills MUST direct agents to (1) describe sites exactly as the site queries select them, (2) state as an obligation any convention the queries rely on, and (3) state only per-site obligations that a reviewer can check from the site and the helpers it calls.

None of these clauses names a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface to delegate through. Each one constrains what the skill text says, which is observable content. The bundle could be built in many ways, such as one file or several, or a different section layout, and still satisfy all three clauses. So no clause is a structural obligation, and no implementation root needs an `{impl}` marker.

The supplied root `assets/skills/habeas/references/distributed-requirements.md` does carry the guidance, as a check on content:
- The Do list says "Describe sites exactly as the site queries select them".
- The same item says to state a convention such as how a variable is named "as an obligation".
- The Don't list says not to state a per-site obligation that "a reviewer cannot check from the site and the helpers it calls", and gives the example "not reported by another check".

Tests supply the evidence for the behavioral content, so no structural gap exists.

behavioral: The requirement has three obligations for the bundled skills. They must direct agents to (1) describe sites exactly as the site queries select them, (2) state as an obligation any convention the queries rely on, such as how a list is named, and (3) state only per-site obligations a reviewer can check from the site and the helpers it calls.

The test is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_describe_sites_as_queries_select_them_with_checkable_obligations]`. It reads the habeas skill's `references/distributed-requirements.md` through `distributed_reference`. It extracts the `## Do` and `## Don't` sections with `section`, which skips code fences and collapses whitespace. It asserts the text with `assert_text`, which checks `contains` and fails with a message.

- **Obligations 1 and 2:** The `## Do` section must contain "Describe sites exactly as the site queries select them. When a query relies on a convention, such as how a variable is named, state the convention as an obligation". That covers the exact-description direction and the convention-as-obligation direction together.
- **Obligation 1, converse:** The `## Don't` section must contain "Don't describe sites more broadly than the queries select".
- **Obligation 3:** The `## Don't` section must contain "Don't state a per-site obligation that a reviewer cannot check from the site and the helpers it calls".

I found the guidance text only in the habeas skill's distributed-requirements reference. A search of `assets/skills` for the related wording found no other skill carrying it, so I found no other skill that would need its own assertion. The test is marked `{test}` for the subject. The phrase assertions would fail if the guidance were removed or reworded to lose any of the three directions. This is guidance text rather than runtime logic, so I found no further observable behaviour to test.
